summary:
## Verdict

**Critical XSS regression** — this change removes the only HTML escaping on comment bodies and feeds the raw string into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

## Narrative

`Comment` previously escaped `&`, `<`, and `>` before assigning to `__html`, which made the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` path safe for plain text. The diff deletes `escapeHtml` and passes `body` through unchanged. Any comment author (or anyone who can influence `body`) can inject arbitrary HTML/JS that runs in every viewer’s session — session theft, UI rewrite, credential exfiltration.

The comment claims “rich formatting (bold/links),” but there is no markdown parser and no allowlist sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify). Unfiltered HTML is not a formatting feature; it is an open XSS sink.

## Release decision

Do not merge until comment HTML is either (a) rendered as React text/nodes from a vetted markdown pipeline, or (b) sanitized with a strict allowlist before `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and passes unsanitized body into dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so any HTML/JS in comment content executes in viewers’ browsers. That is a real stored-XSS regression from the prior escaped plain-text behavior.
